content.comment_body: Hello everyone, hope you're all well. I'm seeking advice on how to create an adjustable timer and counter program to control an output on my [product_name] [article_no]. I want to adjust: how long the output stays on (0-10 seconds), how long it's off (2-180 seconds), and how many on/off cycles occur before stopping (0-10 cycles). I plan to use 8 pushbuttons as inputs for: increasing/decreasing on-time, increasing/decreasing off-time, increasing/decreasing cycle count, starting the program, and stopping/resetting the program. As a beginner, I'm struggling with timers and suspect I'm missing something simple. Any help would be appreciated.
Are you sure the ranges should be 0-10 seconds and 0-10 cycles? Or should it be 1-10 seconds and 1-10 cycles?
I've attached a possible solution. On time: 1-10 seconds, off time: 2-180 seconds, cycles: 1-10.
Thanks for your help, I will try this out and let you know how it goes.
You didn't specify which [product_name] [article_no] model you have. The example I provided was made for the first generation of [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: A beginner user is looking for help with setting up adjustable timers and counters to control output cycles on a [product_name] device. The user faces challenges managing timings and logic with multiple input buttons. Another community member clarifies parameter limits and shares an example design, demonstrating active support, but reveals the user's uncertainty about their exact device model and configuration details.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for straightforward instructions or examples to set up adjustable timers and counters using pushbuttons, enabling easy and reliable control of output cycles suitable for someone new to this type of programming.
